notes:
I don't have any notes on Amos 7 for you yet. I didn't manage to read a single source page, so I can't give you anything I could back up with a URL.

**What went wrong:**
1. My first attempt tried to fetch eight pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary, Wesley and Matthew Henry on biblehub.com, plus the NET Bible notes. That went over the tool's usage limit and returned nothing.
2. I then tried Enduring Word alone. It returned something I couldn't open, and the error that followed meant I never saw what it was.
3. By the time I went to check what it was, I had used up all my tool calls for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to leave gaps rather than fill them from memory. So I've written nothing rather than guess at what Gill, Ellicott or anyone else said about the locusts, the plumb line or Amaziah.

**Next turn, I'll fetch one page per call, in this order:**
1. **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word (David Guzik), Precept Austin, and on biblehub.com the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Matthew Henry and Wesley commentaries.
2. **Where traditions differ:** Wesley's Notes for the Methodist view, plus Ligonier or The Gospel Coalition (Reformed), Desiring God (Baptist) and LCMS (Lutheran). The verses most likely to split them are vv. 3 and 6, on God "relenting," and vv. 14–15, on Amos's calling outside the prophetic guilds.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on the sycamore figs, the "seer" title and the "I was not a prophet" wording; Bible Odyssey on Amos and Bethel; and New Advent or Catholic.com for Catholic readings.

Just reply "continue" and I'll start. If you'd like a smaller first batch, such as Enduring Word and Gill only, say so and I'll begin there.
